resources.string: Telegram without a VPN, and a check of what your network blocks
Turn the Telegram proxy on or off
Proxy on 127.0.0.1:%1$d. Tap \"Connect in Telegram\" once, after that Telegram uses it by itself.
Tap the button: Tropa starts a proxy on this phone that takes Telegram around the block, on Wi-Fi and mobile data.
Telegram goes through Tropa. Tap to open.
Checks YouTube and Discord stage by stage, the same way Tropa does on a PC, and tells how the connection is cut.
No internet at all: this is not a block.
YouTube and Discord through your PC

Android does not let an app bypass blocks for other apps without a VPN. If Tropa runs on your computer, turn on \"For the whole home\" there, then on the phone open Wi-Fi → your network → Proxy → Auto and paste the PAC address that Tropa shows.

If the check says DNS gives a fake address, set Private DNS to one.one.one.one or dns.google. It encrypts DNS for the whole phone. It is usually under \"Network & internet\" or \"Connection & sharing\" → \"Private DNS\".
Address copied. In Wi-Fi settings: your network → Proxy → Auto, paste it into the URL field.
